name: Goi nhong ong
summary: Gỏi nhộng ong is a salad of young bee pupae from the U Minh honey harvest. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam names it with grilled snakehead, honey, lẩu mắm, and eel stewed with nhàu leaves.
origin: U Minh Hạ. Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says the pupae were a forest dish for a long time and now sit on visitor meals.
culture: Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam says that when the honey is taken, the keeper cuts a little young comb, called dọn tàn, so the colony can go on. That comb is the start of the dish.
howToEat: Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam boils the young comb so the wax melts and the pupae rise, then skims them out to drain before cooking.
Cục Du lịch Quốc gia Việt Nam names batter-frying and mắm ong as other plates of the same pupae, and singles out nhộng ong trộn bắp chuối. A price was not printed. Check on arrival.
where: U Minh Hạ, on a forest day. No restaurant is named. Check on arrival.
